recognize_zh: 臨床照片：足踝上方皮膚乾燥、有細紋，可見一個小型、邊界清楚的黑色結痂/壞死性潰瘍，周圍呈發亮的淡色邊緣；此外觀本身不具特異性，需結合 LPL 與冷凝球蛋白血症病史，考慮血管炎或缺血性皮膚病灶。
features: Clinical photograph of the lower leg just above the ankle
Single small, well-demarcated ulcer covered by a black necrotic eschar
Surrounding thin, shiny, pale rim of epidermis without marked erythema in this image
Background skin is dry and xerotic with fine scaling
No palpable purpura or livedo visible in this field; morphology is nonspecific
describe_en: Clinical photograph of the distal lower leg shows a small, sharply demarcated ulcer covered by black necrotic eschar with a thin shiny perilesional rim, on a background of dry, finely scaling skin. No surrounding purpura or livedo reticularis is evident in this image. The lesion is nonspecific; in a patient with lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma and cryoglobulins it is compatible with a cryoglobulinemic or hyperviscosity-related ischemic/vasculitic skin ulcer, and biopsy would be needed to separate vasculitis, vessel-occlusive cryoglobulin deposition or specific cutaneous lymphoma infiltration.

ddx.vs: Specific infiltration typically forms papules, plaques or nodules and shows a dermal lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate on biopsy rather than necrotic eschar.
Stasis ulcers are shallow, on the medial malleolus, with hemosiderin hyperpigmentation and lipodermatosclerosis.
Arterial ulcers are punched-out over pressure points with absent pulses and hairless atrophic skin, without cryoglobulin deposits.
Calciphylaxis shows retiform purpura evolving to eschar, typically in renal failure, with vascular calcification on biopsy.
